title: Ohm's Law Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav's phone charges slowly with a long, thin cable and faster with a short, thick one. Same charger, so what is the thin cable doing? In this animated lesson we see resistance from the inside (electrons bumping into vibrating atoms) and then discover Ohm's law on a live breadboard.

A variable supply steps from 2 V to 8 V while the ammeter and voltmeter read the current and voltage, and every reading is plotted live on a V against I graph: a straight line through zero whose slope is the resistance. Swap in a resistor twice as big and the new line is twice as steep. We state Ohm's law (Georg Simon Ohm, 1827), derive V = IR and R = V/I, define the ohm, meet ohmic and non ohmic parts, and find what decides a wire's resistance: R = ρL/A. Then a worked example, the exam trap (R does not depend on V), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question on a stretched wire with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 8 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 2: Principles of Electricity, Network Theorems and AC Principles (Karnataka PUC Electronics).

2:34 Worked example
